faq.q: How many sunsets do astronauts see a day?
faq.a: The International Space Station goes around Earth about every 90 minutes. So astronauts on board see about 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets every 24 hours.
asks: How many sunrises are there on the ISS?
How fast does the space station orbit?

faq.q: Why is the atmosphere a thin blue line?
faq.a: Most of the air is packed close to the ground: half of it lies within about 5.5 kilometres. Seen edge-on from space, that thin layer scatters blue light into a glowing line.
asks: Why does the air look blue from space?

faq.a: In space there is almost no air, so nothing scatters sunlight towards your eyes. Without scattering, the sky stays black even when the Sun is shining.
asks: Why is space dark if the Sun is shining?
Why is the sky black on the Moon?

faq.q: How long does a sunset last from space?
faq.a: Because the station moves at about 28 thousand kilometres an hour, the Sun drops below Earth's edge very fast. The colourful bands are visible for only a few seconds.
asks: How quick is a sunset on the ISS?

faq.q: Do sunsets from space look different from on Earth?
faq.a: Yes. Instead of a coloured sky around you, you see the colours as thin flat bands along Earth's curved edge: black on top, then blue, then orange and red near the clouds.
asks: What colours do astronauts see at sunset?
What does the edge of Earth look like?

facts: The International Space Station orbits Earth about every 90 minutes, so its crew sees about 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets a day.
About half of all the air in the atmosphere lies within about 5.5 kilometres of sea level.

quiz.say: About how many sunsets do astronauts on the International Space Station see each day?
quiz.show: Sunsets per day on the ISS:
quiz.why: The station circles Earth about every 90 minutes, and 24 hours holds 16 of those orbits.

wrong.0: One sunset a day is what we see on the ground, where Earth turns once a day.
wrong.2: That would need an orbit every 15 minutes, far faster than the station goes.
